title: Composition on the Image of a Computation
statement: Let $M$ and $U$ be finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let $f,g$ be functions from binary words to binary words, and let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ within time $T_1$, and for every binary word $x$, $U$ computes $g(x)$ on input $f(x)$ within time $T_2(|x|)$. Then there is a finite Turing machine that computes $g$ within time $n\mapsto 2T_1(n)+T_2(n)+2$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ and $U$ are finite Turing machines over the binary alphabet
$f,g$ map binary words to binary words
For every $x$, $U$ computes $g(x)$ on input $f(x)$ within time $T_2(|x|)$
replaced:
Let $M$ and $U$ be finite multi-tape Turing machines over the binary alphabet, let
$f, g$ be functions on binary strings, and let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.
If $M$ computes $f$ within $T_1$, and for every input $x$ the machine $U$ run on $f(x)$
halts within $T_2(|x|)$ steps with output $g(x)$, then some finite machine computes $g$
within time $n \mapsto 2\,T_1(n) + T_2(n) + 2$.
